One primary concept each, checked for duplicates. Q1 ligand–receptor interaction set against enzyme–substrate interaction · Q2 signal amplification distinguished from enzyme activation · Q3 the G-protein switch and how a signal is terminated · Q4 the nature and roles of second messengers · Q5 receptor tyrosine kinase activation, and GPLR against RTK point for point · Q6 insulin and glucagon regulating blood glucose through their two receptor classes · Q7 the cellular response as a change in gene expression, and why two cells differ. No concept is the primary target of two questions.

Traps deliberately planted, every one traceable to a real reject line, examiner comment or specimen question. Amplification confused with activation, which is Specimen P1 Q22 exactly. The GDP said to be phosphorylated to become GTP, which is the most repeated reject in this chapter's the papers. A receptor's binding site called an active site, and the enzyme vocabulary that follows it. Phosphorylation assumed always to activate, when the chapter's own figure has protein kinase A phosphorylating glycogen synthase to inhibit it. Yes/no comparisons of the two receptor types, rejected in writing by two schemes. Tyrosine kinase used interchangeably with tyrosine residue. Cyclic AMP treated as a ligand for a cell surface receptor, which caught over 40% of one cohort. Glucagon said to act on skeletal muscle, which is your own chapter's error on pages 36, 37 and 41. A data answer given without quoting the data.
